abstract: Background: The yak (Bos grunniens) is an essential livestock species in high-altitude alpine ecosystems, serving key roles in meat, milk, and wool production as well as ecological maintenance. However, traditional yak breeding systems face several limitations, including fragmented herd data management, inefficient phenotypic collection, missing pedigree records, and high technical barriers to applying genomic technologies. These factors constrain the widespread application of modern genetic evaluation methods in yak breeding programs. Description: We developed the Yak Genomic Evaluation Platform (YGEP, https://yakbreeding.swun.edu.cn/en/), an integrated digital system for yak genetic selection and herd management. YGEP integrates three core analytical modules: pedigree reconstruction, genotype imputation and genomic breeding value estimation. Benchmarking on 706 yaks showed that GBLUP achieved a prediction accuracy of r = 0.96 for cannon bone circumference (CCB), and KBeagle reached 84.0% imputation accuracy with the combined reference panel. Conclusion: YGEP bridges the gap between advanced genomic analytics and practical yak breeding. By integrating pedigree reconstruction, genotype imputation, and GEBV estimation into a user-friendly cloud platform, YGEP effectively eliminates technical and data bottlenecks. Overall, it provides an accessible, scalable, and standardized solution to advance digital herd management and precision genetic improvement in alpine livestock.
